cs.t: I think the screen is what I look for the most. Its specs needed to be  1080p resolution, >95% DCI-P3 color gamut, prefer OLED, prefer touch-enabled Also mattering was lightweight and easy to travel with (including power supply), respectable battery life, >=16GB RAM, processor preferring performance over price, Thunderbolt or USB4 In a different world, I would want something from an OEM with Linux focus, Coreboot, and repairable, but the screens on all of those machines are trash. Last year I picked up a ASUS Zenbook Flip and slapped NixOS on it. My only complaint is that the body isn’t very rigid and got crack in the glass (not over the display) when my bag fell from a shitty bathroom stall hook.
cs.th: Ask HN: What does one look for in a laptop these days?

cs.t: I have an Asus Zen Book Flip, which is super light. Also, I use xmonad and a vim-style editor, which allows me to work w/o relying on a mouse.
